summary: SSD firmware update blocked during depot repair due to BitLocker/TPM owner change, causing reprovisioning failure
description: During routine depot repair and reprovisioning of returned encrypted laptops we observed repeated failures when applying NVMe/SSD firmware updates. The failures correlate with devices that had BitLocker enabled and where the TPM owner was re-provisioned as part of the repair workflow. Failure mode: firmware tool exits early with device busy / access denied and task sequence stalls in WinPE.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Receive returned device with BitLocker encrypted OS volume.
2) Boot to WinPE from depot imaging station.
3) Run repair task sequence which: re-enrolls device into Azure AD/Intune, reapplies company provisioning profile, and runs vendor SSD firmware updater (Dell/Lenovo FW tools).
4) Observe firmware update step timeout/failure and subsequent task sequence error.
5) Attempt to re-run update: vendor tool reports device locked or unreachable (error codes shown in logs).
logs:
Example error lines copied from depot imaging logs: 
[2026-03-09T08:14:22Z] fwupdate.exe --nvme-update --file NVME_2026_03_09.bin --target 0 --errorCode=0x80070005 --msg='Access denied to device handle'
[2026-03-09T08:14:22Z] TaskSequence: Step 'SSD FW Update' failed (exit 5).
WinPE logs: device enumerated as "Disk 0", but CreateFile on \\?\PhysicalDrive0 returned ACCESS_DENIED (0x5).
On-host PowerShell (after reprovision): manage-bde -status returned 'Conversion Status: Fully Encrypted', but protectors list showed new TPM protector GUID different from original device entry.
TPM event: EventID 15 - TPM ownership change detected during provisioning.
Vendor tool (DellCCTK) output: 'Device busy - NVMe controller report failed'.
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: During repair we run an automated TPM reset / re-provision step (to clear previous owner's keys) which, combined with BitLocker still present on the OS volume, leaves the NVMe device in a state where firmware updater cannot open a raw device handle from WinPE. Possible causes: driver/locking interaction when TPM ownership flags change, or the imaging sequence ordering triggers an I/O quiesce race.
What we checked:
- Reconstructed the depot task sequence in staging and reproduced failure on 3 of 6 test units (models above).
- Verified that suspending BitLocker (manage-bde -protectors -disable) before FW update allows the vendor tool to complete successfully.
- Confirmed that if TPM ownership reset happens after BitLocker is suspended but before firmware step, results are nominal. If TPM reset happens during or immediately before WinPE firmware attempt, update fails.
- Cross-referenced with vendor KBs: Dell/Lenovo note that some NVMe FW update methods require exclusive device access and may be blocked if low-level security state changes occur.
- Looked for similar past ticket: INT-50321 (assetdb mismatch) referenced as related but not the same root cause.

Conclusions: Ordering in the depot runbook is the proximate cause. The repro is deterministic when TPM re-ownership occurs in the same boot cycle as FW update attempt.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Chen (Reporter): Filed after 6 devices failed in last 48h batch. Primary impact is repair throughput; not customer-facing but causes backlogs.

2026-03-10 11:05 - Depot Tech (R. Alvarez): Observed that if we manually suspend BitLocker in WinPE before running fwupdate the step completes. Suspending from Windows pre-boot didn't help if TPM reset ran afterwards.

2026-03-11 14:40 - Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Reproduced in staging. Created minimal TS: Re-enroll -> TPM reset -> fw update (FAIL). Re-enroll -> suspend BitLocker -> fw update (PASS). Adding note to hold TPM reset until after FW update as workaround.

2026-03-12 09:30 - Security (N. Patel): Concern about leaving BitLocker suspended across reprovisioning. We need to ensure suspend window is minimal and re-enable protections after firmware update and before shipping.

2026-03-13 15:02 - Eng (S. Brooks): Will add detection in imaging-scripts to check for BitLocker status and automatically suspend before fw step. Also adding automatic re-enable and TPM protector re-create after firmware. PR reference added.

2026-03-14 10:20 - Liam O'Connor: Workaround applied on depot: updated TS to suspend BitLocker before FW step and defer TPM reset until after successful FW update. Monitoring next batch. Creating follow-up automation ticket INT-432111 to land script changes and QA.
2026-03-14 11:00 - Depot Lead (K. Robinson): Current mitigation reduced failure rate to zero in 22 devices processed in a trial run. Logging additional metrics for 72h before closure.
resolution_notes:
Mitigation (applied 2026-03-14): Updated depot task sequence to: 1) Detect encrypted OS volume and suspend BitLocker protectors (manage-bde -protectors -disable). 2) Run vendor SSD firmware update in WinPE. 3) Run TPM re-provision / protector re-creation and re-enable BitLocker.
Permanent fix: Engineering to merge imaging-scripts PR to add idempotent suspend/resume helpers and a check that TPM re-ownership does not occur until firmware step completes (INT-432111).
Follow-ups:
- QA to run extended validation on affected models across us-west depot.
- Security to validate that suspend window is logged and limited; add audit entry to Confluence runbook.
- Ops to monitor depot throughput and reopen if regression observed.

If mitigation proves stable after 72h of samples, move ticket to Resolved and file INT-432111 for the automation work and INT-432112 for runbook update review.
